headline: Frankie — the cofounder sweep came back last night and immediately earned its keep: it found money moving that nobody logged. An UNLISTED Meta campaign, "$300 Plan," has been quietly spending 100% of the ad account ($25/day, $13.92 yesterday) on the exact instant-form route we'd shelved — and it is working. For the first time ever we have real consumer leads on record: Thomas Walker in Texas with a phone, Mary Jane in Idaho with a phone, Claudia Nash by email. Every notification says "call fast." Here is the problem: the compliance gate is still 0/7, and the two blockers that bite hardest — TX telephone-solicitor registration (b3) and your CA producer-license # in the marketing email (b7) — are exactly the two the predecessor account was banned for, and the Texas lead is the one holding a phone. So the first instruction of the day is a stop, not a go: do not call anyone until you two answer two questions — was "$300 Plan" launched on purpose, and by whom; and may these three real people be contacted at all while we sit at 0/7. Everything else waits behind that. (Second, quieter story: the sweep's own bridge to your Mac worked — its first artifact since Aug 25 — while the AM brief fired on cron and still wrote nothing, so this PM is the only Aug 28 brief and the fix is per-task local rebuilds, not another credit reload.)
